findings.title: KeyError when existing Integration metadata lacks 'sender'
findings.body: In GitHubInstallation.dispatch, the user-mismatch check does `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` with no guards. `metadata["sender"]` is only populated when the installation webhook fired before build_integration ran (see build_integration, which only adds `sender` if `state.get("sender")` is set). An existing Integration created without a preceding webhook (e.g. created through the pipeline directly, or older rows predating this flow) has no `sender` key, so this line raises KeyError and the user gets a 500 instead of a graceful error page. Same for a `sender` dict without a `login` key. Use `.get()` with explicit handling (e.g. fail closed with the error page) instead.

findings.title: Unhandled exceptions from token exchange and get_user_info
findings.body: In OAuthLoginView.dispatch, `safe_urlopen(...)` and `get_user_info(payload["access_token"])` are not wrapped in error handling. `get_user_info` performs an API call that can raise ApiError (rate limit, 401 for revoked tokens, network errors), and safe_urlopen can raise on connection failures. Any of these will propagate and produce a 500 error page mid-installation instead of the intended 'Invalid installation request.' response, degrading the UX the PR is meant to fix and generating noise in Sentry. The existing try/except only covers the response body parsing, not the requests themselves.

findings.title: Reverse URL built with None installation_id
findings.body: When GitHub redirects to the setup endpoint with setup_action=install but without an installation_id query parameter (malformed or crafted request), `request.GET.get("installation_id")` returns None and `reverse("integration-installation", args=[provider_id, None])` renders a URL ending in '/github/None'. The user is then redirected to an org-picker URL containing the literal string 'None', which will fail downstream when the pipeline tries to use it. The None case should be handled explicitly (redirect to the app install page or an error) rather than passed into reverse.

findings.title: State signature compared with non-constant-time equality
findings.body: The CSRF/anti-replay `state` parameter is validated with `request.GET.get("state") != pipeline.signature`, a plain string comparison. Since this check is the core of the request-authenticity guarantee introduced by this PR, use `hmac.compare_digest` (or `secrets.compare_digest`) so the comparison is constant-time, matching how other OAuth state validations are typically hardened. Practical exploitability is low, but it is a trivial hardening for a security-focused change.

findings.title: Authorize URL query parameters are not URL-encoded
findings.body: The redirect URL is built by string interpolation: `f"{...}?client_id={github_client_id}&state={state}&redirect_uri={redirect_uri}"`. The `redirect_uri` value (containing '://' and '/'), `client_id`, and `state` are not URL-encoded. This currently works because the values happen to contain no '&' or '=' characters, but any change to the redirect path or a client_id containing reserved characters would silently corrupt the OAuth request. Use `urlencode` to construct the query string.
